authority apart from censure after judicial process (BCO 36-1).

BCO 36-1 doesn't pertain to approving calls or transfers and does not directly bear on the facts of this case. Other than BCO 31-2, it was the only BCO paragraph cited by the SJC, and it was the chief citation.

artifacts.synopsis: Great Lakes Presbytery erred in approving Recommendation 5 of its Judicial Commission's report, which preemptively stated that Presbytery would not recommend or transfer TE Gonzales if he declined to demit or step away from ministry, because such action exceeded Presbytery's authority apart from censure after due judicial process.

artifacts.title: Sherfey v. James River Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Sherfey's complaint against James River Presbytery was ruled judicially out of order with defects that cannot be cured, because the bases of his complaint had not been adjudicated by JRP as required by BCO 43-2, and because the complaint to the General Assembly was not timely filed within the 30-day period of BCO 43-3. A concurring opinion by RE Duncan and RE Burnett noted that JRP's commission gave de novo review beyond the Record of the Case and should have narrowly adjudicated whether JRP erred in denying the original complaint.

artifacts.synopsis: Dr. Robert Shive appealed his conviction and excommunication after Christ Covenant Church found him guilty of sinful and sexually inappropriate speech toward two patients. The SJC found no reversible error in the trial, but held that the record did not show contumacy or impenitence sufficient for excommunication, reversed that censure, and remanded for indefinite suspension from the sacraments under BCO 36-5; a dissent was recorded.

artifacts.title: Shive v. Central Carolina
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC reversed the session's imposition of excommunication on Dr. Robert Shive for inappropriate conduct while counseling female patients, remanding instead for indefinite suspension from the Sacraments, finding insufficient evidence of contumacy or impenitence to justify the highest censure.
